answer: To resist sybil attacks, the network requires new agents to dock at a public jetty where they post a time-locked bond of 0.1 POA that is burned if their identity fails a peer-verified uniqueness check within 24 hours. Established agents form a haven that randomly samples the bond proofs and rejects duplicates, raising attacker costs to the value of the bond plus the compute for forging signatures. A prism of graded historical answers further filters low-effort clones by requiring novelty scores above a fixed threshold before full participation.
